provided_deck_matrix_assessment: The active representative matrix contains 11 decks: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, Kingslayer, Boarlock, and PirateDH.

The matrix stage split is explicit and current: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, and PirateDH are core_source_backed_fixture rows; Kingslayer and Boarlock are source_informed_valid_fixture rows.

The representative deck set covers major pre-run families without excessive fixture bloat: aggro burn, hero-power transform, recruit board flood, pirate tempo, weapon pressure, big recruit/deathrattle cheat, discard, token board snowball, hero-power spell generation, mech scaling, combo-control, and hero-attack pressure.

Kingslayer is preserved as a source-informed weapon-sequence control because exact Kingslayer/Kingsbane Quick Pick mulligan evidence remains unavailable; its stop condition is exact_kingslayer_quick_pick_mulligan_source_unavailable.

Boarlock is preserved as a source-informed combo-control control because exact Boarlock-relevant Fracking mulligan evidence and lowering blockers remain; its stop condition is exact_boarlock_fracking_mulligan_source_unavailable.

Boarlock remains useful even while source-informed because it is the representative Combo.json control row, but the docs correctly avoid treating the low-confidence Fracking row as source-backed strong.

CuteWarrior is listed in docs/operator/supplemental-proof-decks.json as supplemental_load_safe_only, with representative_output_competence=false. That is the right role: it proves narrow acceptance/load-safety behavior without becoming a twelfth representative source-depth row.

The matrix is broad enough for current no-block regression confidence but intentionally not exhaustive. Dedicated secret, freeze, location, questline, discover-control, overload-first, board-position, generic spell-target, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter deck families are mostly covered by policy and unit tests rather than by named representative rows.

The matrix governance is healthy because it refuses to add decks merely to avoid honest source-depth gaps. Existing source-informed rows must either receive exact source evidence or remain visible with explicit stop conditions.

The provided deck set supports the audit conclusion that HSConfig is competent for a lean pre-run package generator. It does not support a stronger claim that every Wild mechanic is source-backed, optimized, or fixture-proven.
no_block_assessment: The safe no-block meaning is technical and load-safety based: a valid normal-path deck package that decodes, resolves required identity, validates JSON structure, emits required minimal runtime files, and passes the operator summary gate should not be blocked by semantic warning debt.

Minimal load-safe apply is deliberately narrower than normal prepare richness: GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json are the required runtime files. Per-card CARDID.json files are normal HSConfig rich output and matrix proof, but not the minimal runtime-write gate.

SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG remains a confidence and handoff label. It means current source coverage and per-card closure are strong enough to call the package source-backed; it is not required for load_safe_apply.

VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG and STATIC_SEMANTICS_USABLE can still be valid load-safe states when technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE and runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply. Their warnings tell the operator what to inspect, not that runtime write is blocked.

Warnings that should remain non-blocking for valid load-safe packages include missing guide claims, generic-low-confidence cards, source-depth gaps, missing exact mulligan claims, missing combo sequence detail, runtime-surface gaps that stay report-only, unsupported claims that are suppressed, partial mechanics, warning-only mechanics, text-only mechanics, unknown mechanics, unknown card types, and load_safe_but_thin config usefulness.

Hard blocks are still real and technical: malformed or unsupported deckcode, unresolved required identity, invalid JSON, unsupported VisionAI filenames or blocks, GameCardId mismatches, malformed Mulligan or Combo rows, missing GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, missing input_manifest.json, missing operator_summary.json, nested runtime files, undeclared runtime files, normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json, forged apply gates, stale fake receipts, and runtime drift before receipt application.

The apply path is no-block only after a valid package exists. `hsconfig apply --json` revalidates package structure and the operator summary gate, creates or verifies fake receipt evidence, then writes when allowed.

The no-block claim should not be expanded into gameplay quality. It does not prove winrate improvement, matchup optimization, replay-backed correctness, exact future mechanic support, exact combo timing for every deck, or exact mulligan confidence for every deck.
The repo currently expresses the right product boundary: valid normal-path packages should keep moving, while confidence debt remains visible in operator_summary.json and lower-level reports.
skill_slimness_assessment: The installed skill is slim enough for use as an operator workflow. It gives one normal path, starts at docs/operator/README.md, reads operator_summary.json first, and treats lower-level commands and optional inputs as expert or diagnostic paths.

The skill is efficient because heavy deterministic work lives in the Python package, tests, reports, and reference docs; the skill itself mostly routes the operator through source evidence, prepare, validate, summary inspection, and optional apply.
The skill avoids HSranger/HSTuner scope creep. It repeatedly excludes replay analysis, winrate analysis, runtime-log analysis, candidate promotion, HSTuner follow-up, and after-game tuning.

The skill is competent because it names the important runtime surfaces, explains source document normalization, keeps exact CardID identity, requires full GlobalValues coverage and profiling, and directs operators to the right reports for source-depth, claim-gap, strong-promotion, mechanic-drift, and config-usefulness inspection.

The skill is honest about source-confidence debt. It preserves VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG, semantic_blockers, guide_strength_summary, source_claim_gap_report.json, strong_promotion_report.json, and the Kingslayer/Boarlock stop conditions instead of forcing weak source claims into SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG.

The skill correctly treats config_usefulness as a non-blocking explanation layer. It tells the operator to report the first gap and next_report_to_open without switching to HSTuner or replay analysis inside HSConfig.

The skill correctly treats modern mechanic visibility as descriptive. It names direct, identity-gated direct, partial, and warning-only buckets and says warning-only mechanics must not block load_safe_apply for technically valid packages.

The skill is dense in a few sections, but most density is protective wording around common confusion points: source-informed compatibility, per-card rich output versus minimal apply, mechanic warning visibility, and source-backed strong promotion. That density is acceptable and preferable to an over-broad or optimistic skill.
hearthstone_semantic_coverage: Card identity coverage is suitable for pre-run package generation: package_builder.py builds deck identity, card metadata, source claim bundles, gameplan contracts, identity graph reports, deck fingerprints, and candidate archetype reports before runtime config compilation.

The normal runtime surface coverage is bounded and clear: GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, per-card CARDID.json files, and optional Combo.json for concrete valid combos. Presume.json and Concede.json are known surfaces but blocked from normal apply.

Direct runtime-lowerable mechanics include common action families such as battlecry, damage, discard, hero_power, overkill, overload, and weapon, with discover, choose_one, and hero_power_transform treated as identity-gated direct because exact option or transformed identity must be source-backed.

Partial mechanics include broad static or posture families where only part of the behavior maps safely to existing VisionAI rows, such as generated_entity, freeze, destroy, silence, transform, secret, location, questline, imbue, spellburst, miniaturize, quickdraw, honorable_kill, elusive, poisonous, recruit, deathrattle, aura, divine_shield, rush, charge, spell_damage, start_of_game, highlander, plague, invoke, jade, cthun_package, and spell_school.

Warning-only mechanics include known no-runtime-row or no-safe-generic-lowering families such as board_position, generic_spell_target, location_activation, secret_timing, generated_entity_random_pool, dredge, tradeable, kindred, tourist, starship, rewind, herald, shatter, outcast, forge, and titan.

Mechanic drift is handled as non-blocking visibility. Unknown mechanics, text-only mechanics, and unknown card types are surfaced in mechanic_drift_report.json and summarized in operator_summary.json, but they do not block load_safe_apply for a technically valid package.

Choice-surface handling is appropriately conservative: discover_choice and choose_one_choice lower only when option identity is source-backed; unresolved option identity is retained in card_behavior_suppression_report.json.

Combo support is intentionally exacting. Combo.json is emitted only when combo_sequence claims include explicit sequence, timing_kind, operator, and values; incomplete combo claims remain report-visible.

GlobalValues coverage is strong for pre-run posture, not runtime tuning. Baseline keys are loaded and profiled, copy_baseline keys are preserved, source-backed Step1 posture overlays may change selected keys, and runtime_evidence_required keys stay blocked until a runtime-evidence workflow owns them.
The semantic coverage is enough for a no-block load-safe package generator. It is not complete first-class gameplay modeling for every Hearthstone mechanic, and it should not be presented that way.
gaps_or_risks: The full pytest suite was not executed in this audit because the task permitted reading repo files and tests and required writing only the requested JSON file. The audit therefore does not assert a current full-suite pass.
The current no-block proof is strong implementation-contract evidence, not a mathematical proof over every possible valid future deckcode or future Hearthstone mechanic.

The representative matrix does not directly fixture every mechanic family. Dedicated secret, freeze, location, questline, discover-control, overload-first, board-position, generic spell-target, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter coverage is mostly policy/unit-test coverage rather than named representative deck coverage.
Warning-only mechanic handling is correct for load safety, but decks centered on warning-only mechanics may produce strategically thin packages until exact source-backed runtime surfaces exist.

The CLI still exposes expert and legacy surfaces such as build, research-contract, --cards-json, --claims-json, --plan-reports-dir, --allow-placeholder, and --allow-source-informed. They are documented as expert or compatibility paths, but can still confuse new operators.

Older docs/research result folders can contain superseded claims. Active docs and tests now guard the main stale matrix-count phrasing, but broad searches across all research history may still surface outdated context.

Per-card every-card output is both normal prepare behavior and repo rich-output proof, but it is not the minimal runtime-write gate or an official HearthRanger minimum. Operators who skip the docs may conflate these concepts.
load_safe_apply is an HSConfig operator policy term, not a public HearthRanger term. That distinction is documented, but it remains important when communicating externally.

The apply gate depends on operator_summary.json generated_files consistency and package structure. That is good safety behavior, but stale or hand-edited packages will correctly block even when a human expects apply to trust summary fields alone.
recommended_next_action: Keep the core apply gate and skill workflow unchanged. The highest-leverage small polish is to keep the active-doc stale-claim guard in place and, if future edits touch docs again, extend it only narrowly around old matrix-count or source-informed wording rather than adding more representative decks.
